Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All oranges are apples.

Some oranges are bananas.

All bananas are fruits.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some fruits are apples.

II. Some apples are bananas.

III. Some oranges are fruits.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow.
Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:

Conclusions:

I. Some fruits are apples → Follow (As all oranges are apples, some oranges are bananas and all bananas are fruits. So, as there is some common part between oranges and bananas which whole comes in apples and fruits respectively so some fruits are apples is definitely true) 

II. Some apples are bananas → Follow (As As all oranges are apples and some oranges are bananas. So, as bananas has some common part with oranges which whole comes in apples therefore some apples are bananas is definitely true)

III. Some oranges are fruits → Follow (As some oranges are bananas and all bananas are fruits. So, as there is some common part between oranges and bananas which whole comes in fruits so some oranges are fruits is definitely true) 

∴ Here,** All conclusions I, II and III follows.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"All conclusions follow.**".

questions.question: In 1931, who recognised that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons, which can mathematically be written as 4n + 2 (n = 0, 1, 2, 3 etc.)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Erich Huckel was a German chemist and physicist.
 
• He proposed a theory in 1931 to help determine if a planar ring molecule would have aromatic properties.
 
• Erich Huckel recognized that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons.
 
• His rule states that a cyclic, planar molecule is considered aromatic if it has 4n+2 pi electrons.
 
• This rule is known as Huckel's Rule.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pi bond:- Bond formed by the same phase overlap of atomic orbitals along a direction perpendicular to the internuclear axis is called pi bond.
 
• Pi electrons:- An electron that resides in the pi bond (s) of a double bond or a triple bond or in a conjugated p orbital is called pi electron.
 
• ​System is divided into aromatic, anti-aromatic, and non-aromatic based on no. of pi electrons-
 
 
• ​​​Aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an aromatic system is determined by N = 4n+2 (n is an integer)
 
• Anti-aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an anti-aromatic system is determined by N = 4n (n is an integer)
 
• Non-aromatic - If a compound does not have a continuous ring of conjugated p orbitals in a planar module, then it is called non-aromatic.

• The set continues until one player/team wins by two games.
 
 
 
• Tiebreak Set
 
 
• In a tiebreak set, a player or team needs to win six games wins a set.
 
• If the score gets to 5-5 (5-all), one player must win the next two games to win the set.

questions.question: Which dynasty bronze statues were made using the “lost wax” technique?

The lost-wax technique (Cire Perdue):

__
 
• Used for making the bronze statues.
 
• In this technique, wax figures are first coated with wet clay and allowed to dry.
 
• The clay coated figures are then heated, allowing the wax inside to melt.
 
• The wax is then poured out through a tiny hole and liquid metal is poured inside the hollow mould.
 
• After the metal has cooled down and solidified, the clay coat is removed and a metal figure of the same shape as the wax figure is obtained.
 
• Chola Dynasty also used this technique to make bronze statues.
